title: Priv EKS control-plane blue/green upgrade policy engine and preflight checks
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and orchestration policy engine to perform blue/green control-plane upgrades for Redwood Private (EKS) clusters. The module will provide automated preflight validations, phased traffic shift (canary → gradual), automated smoke tests, and safe rollback when health checks fail. It must integrate with existing provisioner outputs, KMS-based secrets for upgrade credentials, and the Console rollout dashboard for visibility. This work reduces upgrade blast radius, shortens maintenance windows, and provides auditable decision points for on-prem and VPC deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes inputs/outputs consistent with existing private-eks provisioner and supports blue/green target groups for control-plane endpoints
Preflight validations run as part of plan/apply and fail early with actionable diagnostics (IAM, subnets, AZ capacity, control-plane API reachability)
Policy engine supports canary window (configurable percentage/time), automated smoke tests (kubeapi, kubelet, control-plane metrics), and automated rollback on failure
Module emits structured upgrade events to Console (rollout start, canary pass/fail, full-swap complete) with correlation ID
Playbook & runbook created and linked; GitHub PR for module includes end-to-end tests and example usage for private and dedicated clusters

implementation_plan: 1) Define module inputs/outputs and versioned contract; document breaking changes and migration guidance.
2) Implement blue/green control-plane wiring (parallel endpoint, DNS swap plan), leveraging existing EKS control-plane endpoint abstraction.
3) Build preflight checks as terraform null_resource + external script that returns structured diagnostics
4) Develop policy engine (lightweight controller) that coordinates canary percentage, windows, smoke tests, and rollback decisions. Expose flags to run in fully-automated or manual-approval modes.
5) Integrate with Console telemetry and rollout APIs to surface progress and events.
6) Add CI e2e tests and a grooming runbook; schedule canary on a subset of non-prod clusters before wider rollout.
7) Security review + IAM policy hardening + KMS integration for upgrade secrets.
8) Ship module with example usage and migration notes; monitor first 3 production upgrades closely and collect metrics.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Control-plane DNS swap could create brief API unavailability in misconfigured clusters. Mitigation: implement DNS TTL pre-warm and fail-safe loopback if API checks fail.
Risk: IAM misconfig causing upgrade automation to fail mid-flight. Mitigation: add dry-run IAM check in preflight and fail before instance replacement.
Risk: Smoke tests are not representative of production workloads. Mitigation: allow customer-supplied smoke test scripts and a staged canary that increases traffic gradually.
Risk: Rollout engine has a bug that triggers mass rollback. Mitigation: start with manual-approval mode for first 5 upgrades, enable automatic rollback only after stable runs.
